Source format: Event Plan

The Merlion Sounds Festival 2026 (hereinafter "MSF 2026" or "the Festival") is a one-day, multi-stage music event to be held at The Promontory @ Marina Bay, Singapore. The Festival is organised by Bayfront Events Pte Ltd under the authority of Event Operations Command (EOC). This Event Plan (EP) defines the event scope, schedule, and safety protocols for all staff, contractors, vendors, and volunteers engaged in the delivery of MSF 2026.

The Festival gates will open at 17:00 SGT. The scheduled start of performances is 18:00 SGT on 15 August 2026. The event will conclude with the final act's set ending at 00:30 SGT on 16 August 2026. All times referenced in this document are in Singapore Time (SGT, UTC+8) unless otherwise indicated.

This document is the controlling plan for the event day. Where a conflict exists between this plan and any departmental or contractor plan, this plan takes precedence unless a formal amendment has been issued by EOC. All personnel are required to read and acknowledge this plan prior to commencing work on site.

4. SITE ACCESS & ZONING

4.1 Site Zones
The site is divided into the following zones for operational control. Zone access is controlled by the Security Team and requires the appropriate accreditation.
5.1 Power Supply Overview
Primary power is supplied by two 500 kVA generators located in the Power Yard (Zone C). A third 250 kVA generator is on standby for critical loads (EOC, medical, and stage lighting for the Main Stage). The standby generator is tested daily at 13:00 SGT and 23:00 SGT.

5.2 Load Shedding Protocol
In the event of a generator failure or overload, the EOC may initiate load shedding in the following order:
1. Non-essential vendor stalls (food & beverage, merchandise)
2. Bayfront Stage lighting (after 22:30 SGT)
3. Decorative lighting (walkways, entrance)
4. Main Stage sound (only as a last resort, with Festival Director approval)

All load shedding actions must be logged in the event log with time, zone, and reason.

5.3 Fuel & Refill Schedule
| Time | Activity | Location | Responsible |
|---|---|---|---|
| 14:00 SGT | Primary gen refill | Power Yard | Production Team |
| 02:00 SGT | Primary & standby gen refill | Power Yard | Production Team |

Note: The 02:00 SGT refill occurs after the scheduled end of the festival. This is to ensure generators are at full capacity for the post-event strike and site restoration.

6. CROWD MANAGEMENT & SAFETY

6.1 Crowd Control Measures
- The Main Stage area has a maximum capacity of 8,000 persons. The total site capacity is 15,000 persons.
- Crowd flow rate will be monitored by the EOC via CCTV and entry gate counts. If the dwell time in any zone exceeds 20 minutes, crowd control barriers will be adjusted and additional staff deployed.
- The Waterfront Gate (Gate 2) is the primary exit point for dispersal. In the event of a full site evacuation, both Gates 1 and 2 will be opened, and the public address system will broadcast instructions in English, Mandarin, and Malay.

6.2 Medical & First Aid
- Two medical tents are located: one near the Main Stage (Medical Post A) and one near the Bayfront Stage (Medical Post B).
- Medical Post A is staffed from 17:00 SGT until 01:30 SGT. Medical Post B is staffed from 17:00 SGT until 23:00 SGT.
- Any serious incident (e.g., cardiac arrest, severe trauma) must be reported to the EOC immediately on radio channel 1. The EOC will coordinate with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) if required.

7. CLOSING PROCEDURES & POST-EVENT WRAP-UP

7.1 Scheduled End of Event
Merlion Sounds Festival scheduled_end_local 2026-08-16T00:30:00+08:00. Record status: current.

This is the official end time for all performances and public activities. The EOC will announce the end of the event via the public address system at 00:25 SGT, and the closing set will conclude at 00:30 SGT.

7.2 Dispersal & Site Clearance
- From 00:30 SGT, all attendees must exit the site. Gates 1 and 2 will remain open until 01:00 SGT for egress. No re-entry is permitted after 00:30 SGT.
- The Bayfront Stage area will be cleared of all personnel by 00:45 SGT. The Main Stage area will be cleared by 01:00 SGT.
- Public transport coordination: Additional MRT and bus services have been arranged with the Land Transport Authority for the period 00:30 – 02:00 SGT. Shuttle buses will depart from the designated pick-up point near Gate 2 every 15 minutes.

7.3 Strike & Load-Out
- Strike (dismantling of stages, equipment, and infrastructure) commences at 01:00 SGT on 16 August 2026.
- Load-out vehicles may enter via Gate 3 from 01:00 SGT. Vehicle movement within the site is restricted to the service road and staging areas.
- All contractors must complete their load-out by 12:00 SGT on 16 August 2026. Any contractor requiring an extension must submit a request to the Production Manager by 10:00 SGT on 16 August 2026.

Please note that this permit is issued to Merlion Sounds Festival Pte Ltd and is specific to the
event, dates, and venue stated above. The permit is not transferable. Any change in the event
scope, including but not limited to a change in the number of attendees, the addition of
amplified sound stages, or a change in the layout of the venue, must be submitted to NEA for
re-assessment before the change is implemented.

**1. Event Capacity**

1.1 The Marina Bay Floating Platform has a capacity_people of 27000 people, as stated in the
regulatory approval. This is the maximum number of persons permitted to be present within
the venue at any one time, including audience, staff, performers, crew, and vendors. This
figure is current and is based on the approved site layout and emergency egress plan
certified by the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) on 2 January 2026.

1.2 The event organiser shall implement a crowd management system to ensure that the total
number of persons within the venue does not exceed the capacity stated in Condition 1.1 at
any time. The system shall include, but is not limited to, entry point counting, real-time
monitoring, and a clear communication protocol with the venue management and SCDF.

1.3 The event organiser shall display signs indicating the maximum capacity of the venue at all
public entry points and at the main information counter.

**2. Noise Control**

2.1 The permissible noise level at the boundary of the venue shall not exceed 85 dB(A) over a
5-minute period between 10.00 hours and 22.00 hours. Between 22.00 hours and 07.00
hours, the permissible noise level shall not exceed 65 dB(A) over a 5-minute period.

The Marina Bay Floating Platform has a capacity_people of 27000 people, as stated in the regulatory approval. Record status: current.

2.2 The event organiser shall ensure that all amplified sound, including music, announcements,
and effects, is directed away from residential areas. The main stage speakers shall be
configured in accordance with the Noise Management Plan submitted, which includes the
use of line array systems with directional control.

2.3 The event organiser shall provide a dedicated noise monitoring team to conduct continuous
noise monitoring at the venue boundary and at designated sensitive receptors. The
monitoring results shall be recorded and submitted to NEA within 24 hours of a request
by NEA.

2.4 In the event of a noise complaint, the event organiser shall comply with any directive
issued by NEA, including but not limited to reducing the volume, adjusting the speaker
configuration, or ceasing amplified sound operations.

2.5 The event organiser shall ensure that sound checks and rehearsals are conducted only
between 09.00 hours and 20.00 hours on the days immediately preceding the event dates,
unless prior written approval is obtained from NEA.

**3. Waste Management**

3.1 The event organiser shall implement the Waste Management Plan submitted with the
application. This includes the provision of at least 200 general waste bins, 60 recycling
bins (for recyclables such as plastic bottles, aluminium cans, and paper), and 12 bins for
food waste, distributed across the venue as per the approved layout.

3.2 The event organiser shall engage a licensed waste collector to remove waste from the
venue at least twice daily, or more frequently as needed to prevent overflow. The waste
collector shall be licensed under the Environmental Public Health (General Waste
Disposal) Regulations.

**SCHEDULE – CONDITIONS OF PERMIT**

**1. General Conditions**

1.1 The Organiser shall comply with all applicable requirements of the Environmental
    Public Health Act (Cap. 95), the Environmental Public Health (General Waste

    and the Environmental Protection and Management (Noise) Regulations.

    the layout plan submitted with the application (Drawing No. MSF-2026-LP-Rev B,

1.3 The Organiser shall appoint a designated Environmental Compliance Officer (ECO)

2.2 The Organiser shall maintain a noise monitoring log. The log shall record the
    date, time, monitoring location, measured Leq, and the name of the person
    conducting the monitoring. The log shall be made available to NEA upon request.

2.3 In the event that the noise level at any designated sensitive receptor is found to
    exceed the applicable limit, the Organiser shall take immediate corrective action,
    which may include reducing volume, adjusting speaker configuration, or ceasing
    amplified sound operations until compliance is restored. A report of the
    exceedance and the corrective action taken shall be submitted to NEA within

1. SCOPE
This specification covers the temporary power supply, distribution, and generator requirements for the Bayfront Beats Festival 2026, held over two event days (13–14 June 2026) with load-in commencing 08 June 2026 and strike completed by 17 June 2026. The venue has a permanent shore supply rated at 400 A, 415 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz, available at the main switch room near the east service ramp. 5.1 Power Supply Overview
Primary power is supplied by two 500 kVA generators located in the Power Yard (Zone C). A third 250 kVA generator is on standby for critical loads (EOC, medical, and stage lighting for the Main Stage). The standby generator is tested daily at 13:00 SGT and 23:00 SGT.

5.2 Load Shedding Protocol
In the event of a generator failure or overload, the EOC may initiate load shedding in the following order:
1. Non-essential vendor stalls (food & beverage, merchandise)
2. Bayfront Stage lighting (after 22:30 SGT)
3. Decorative lighting (walkways, entrance)
4. Main Stage sound (only as a last resort, with Festival Director approval)

All load shedding actions must be logged in the event log with time, zone, and reason.

6. CROWD MANAGEMENT & SAFETY

6.1 Crowd Control Measures
- The Main Stage area has a maximum capacity of 8,000 persons. The total site capacity is 15,000 persons.
- Crowd flow rate will be monitored by the EOC via CCTV and entry gate counts. If the dwell time in any zone exceeds 20 minutes, crowd control barriers will be adjusted and additional staff deployed.
- The Waterfront Gate (Gate 2) is the primary exit point for dispersal. In the event of a full site evacuation, both Gates 1 and 2 will be opened, and the public address system will broadcast instructions in English, Mandarin, and Malay.

6.2 Medical & First Aid
- Two medical tents are located: one near the Main Stage (Medical Post A) and one near the Bayfront Stage (Medical Post B).
- Medical Post A is staffed from 17:00 SGT until 01:30 SGT. Medical Post B is staffed from 17:00 SGT until 23:00 SGT.
- Any serious incident (e.g., cardiac arrest, severe trauma) must be reported to the EOC immediately on radio channel 1. The EOC will coordinate with the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) if required.

- From 00:30 SGT, all attendees must exit the site. Gates 1 and 2 will remain open until 01:00 SGT for egress. No re-entry is permitted after 00:30 SGT.
- The Bayfront Stage area will be cleared of all personnel by 00:45 SGT. The Main Stage area will be cleared by 01:00 SGT.
- Public transport coordination: Additional MRT and bus services have been arranged with the Land Transport Authority for the period 00:30 – 02:00 SGT. Shuttle buses will depart from the designated pick-up point near Gate 2 every 15 minutes.

7.3 Strike & Load-Out
- Strike (dismantling of stages, equipment, and infrastructure) commences at 01:00 SGT on 16 August 2026.
- Load-out vehicles may enter via Gate 3 from 01:00 SGT. Vehicle movement within the site is restricted to the service road and staging areas.
- All contractors must complete their load-out by 12:00 SGT on 16 August 2026. Any contractor requiring an extension must submit a request to the Production Manager by 10:00 SGT on 16 August 2026.

Please note that this permit is issued to Merlion Sounds Festival Pte Ltd and is specific to the
event, dates, and venue stated above. The permit is not transferable. Any change in the event
scope, including but not limited to a change in the number of attendees, the addition of
amplified sound stages, or a change in the layout of the venue, must be submitted to NEA for
re-assessment before the change is implemented.

**1. Event Capacity**

1.1 The Marina Bay Floating Platform has a capacity_people of 27000 people, as stated in the
regulatory approval. This is the maximum number of persons permitted to be present within
the venue at any one time, including audience, staff, performers, crew, and vendors. This
figure is current and is based on the approved site layout and emergency egress plan
certified by the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) on 2 January 2026.

1.2 The event organiser shall implement a crowd management system to ensure that the total
number of persons within the venue does not exceed the capacity stated in Condition 1.1 at
any time. The system shall include, but is not limited to, entry point counting, real-time
monitoring, and a clear communication protocol with the venue management and SCDF.

1.3 The event organiser shall display signs indicating the maximum capacity of the venue at all
public entry points and at the main information counter.

**2. Noise Control**

2.1 The permissible noise level at the boundary of the venue shall not exceed 85 dB(A) over a
5-minute period between 10.00 hours and 22.00 hours. Between 22.00 hours and 07.00
hours, the permissible noise level shall not exceed 65 dB(A) over a 5-minute period.

The Marina Bay Floating Platform has a capacity_people of 27000 people, as stated in the regulatory approval. Record status: current.

2.2 The event organiser shall ensure that all amplified sound, including music, announcements,
and effects, is directed away from residential areas. The main stage speakers shall be
configured in accordance with the Noise Management Plan submitted, which includes the
use of line array systems with directional control.

2.3 The event organiser shall provide a dedicated noise monitoring team to conduct continuous
noise monitoring at the venue boundary and at designated sensitive receptors. The
monitoring results shall be recorded and submitted to NEA within 24 hours of a request
by NEA.

2.4 In the event of a noise complaint, the event organiser shall comply with any directive
issued by NEA, including but not limited to reducing the volume, adjusting the speaker
configuration, or ceasing amplified sound operations.

2.5 The event organiser shall ensure that sound checks and rehearsals are conducted only
between 09.00 hours and 20.00 hours on the days immediately preceding the event dates,
unless prior written approval is obtained from NEA.

**3. Waste Management**

3.1 The event organiser shall implement the Waste Management Plan submitted with the
application. This includes the provision of at least 200 general waste bins, 60 recycling
bins (for recyclables such as plastic bottles, aluminium cans, and paper), and 12 bins for
food waste, distributed across the venue as per the approved layout.

3.2 The event organiser shall engage a licensed waste collector to remove waste from the
venue at least twice daily, or more frequently as needed to prevent overflow. The waste
collector shall be licensed under the Environmental Public Health (General Waste
Disposal) Regulations.

documents.content:
POWER LOAD PLAN v3 – TECHNICAL SPECIFICATION
Event: Bayfront Beats Festival 2026
Venue: The Meadow, Marina Bay Floating Platform
Document Ref: BBF26-PLP-v3
Revision: 3 (current)
Date Issued: 12 May 2026
Author: Technical Director, Bayfront Beats
Status: APPROVED FOR LOAD-IN

Revision History
Rev 0 – 02 Mar 2026 – Initial draft for site survey.
Rev 1 – 18 Mar 2026 – Updated after vendor RFI; added gen set B contingency.
Rev 2 – 20 Apr 2026 – Revised after fire safety audit; changed cable routing for Stage B.
Rev 3 – 12 May 2026 – Final load calculations, generator de-rate factors, and distribution board schedule. The Power Load Plan v3 version is v3, as specified in the technical specification. Record status: current. This revision supersedes Rev 2 and is the current controlled document for all power distribution work.

1. SCOPE
This specification covers the temporary power supply, distribution, and generator requirements for the Bayfront Beats Festival 2026, held over two event days (13–14 June 2026) with load-in commencing 08 June 2026 and strike completed by 17 June 2026. It applies to all stages, back-of-house (BOH) areas, production offices, catering, and site lighting. All contractors, vendors, and stage crews must refer to this document for connection points, load limits, and cable sizing. Any deviation from this plan requires written approval from the Technical Director.

2. SITE POWER OVERVIEW
The venue has a permanent shore supply rated at 400 A, 415 V, 3-phase, 50 Hz, available at the main switch room near the east service ramp. This shore supply will serve the production compound and BOH areas. All stage power will be provided by diesel generators positioned along the west perimeter, away from audience flow paths. The generators are to be installed on timber cribbing and acoustic blankets, with fuel containment trays rated for 110% of the tank capacity. Refuelling is scheduled for 06:00 daily, before crowd arrival.

The distribution philosophy is a radial system from each generator to its stage distro, with no paralleling of generators. Each stage operates as an independent island. The shore supply feeds a single site distro board, which then feeds BOH sub-distribution. There is no auto-transfer switching between shore and generator supplies. Changeover is a manual plug-and-cable operation, carried out only during non-performance hours.

3. GENERATOR SCHEDULE
All generators are rated for continuous duty at 40°C ambient. De-rating factors have been applied per the manufacturer's data. The festival operates in a tropical climate; therefore, all generator ratings in this plan are de-rated by 12% from the nameplate prime rating. The calculated load for each generator must not exceed 80% of the de-rated capacity. This margin accounts for harmonic content from LED walls and switching power supplies, as well as future additions during the event.
